about: When a TradeComply result needs a licensed or certified person: which tool output triggers it, who, why (the legal basis and the rulebook rules behind it), and when. Professional types and official directories come from tradecomply/data/professionals.json; extra_types adds the types that file does not have yet. TradeComply never recommends, ranks or picks a person or firm.
source: The handoff map in docs/product.md section 4, re-checked on 2026-11-26 by running every entry's test against fresh tool output with a strict evaluator (a missing field is an error).

fields.test: Expression over `result` (the tool's structured output; dict keys read as attributes) and `args` (the tool's inputs). Evaluated by tradecomply/professionals.py with a restricted evaluator, never eval of arbitrary code.
fields.requirement: required | conditional (only if a fact the tool flags is true) | recommended | optional. Only required and conditional are legal requirements.
fields.registry_type_id: The professionals.json type that holds the directories (null: see extra_types).
fields.rule_status: Status of each rule id in the rulebook when the map was checked; the live status is read from tradecomply/data/rulebook.json.
fields.rulebook_verified: Every rule id was confirmed or corrected when the map was checked.
fields.basis_complete: False when part of the legal basis is not backed by a verified rulebook rule (marked 'not yet confirmed' in legal_basis_plain); such an entry is never shown as verified.
fields.due_field: Dotted path to an ISO date in the tool result that answers 'when'.
fields.prefer_find: The directory URL to show for this entry when its type lists several.
fields.role_find: The directory URL to show first for a role (default: the type's first link).
fields.link_scopes: Directory pages run by one city or district: label, and county/city when the page only serves that place (never shown as the link for a job elsewhere).
fields.why / when_plain / legal_basis_plain: Plain-English text shown to people (legal_basis_plain only where legal_basis has notes meant for developers).
fields.conditional_if: Optional test for a 'required' entry: when it holds for a result (the tool itself left a deciding fact open, e.g. its own status for the item is 'conditional'), or cannot be read, the item is shown as 'conditional' instead of 'required'.

extra_types.name: Physician or other licensed health care professional (PLHCP)
extra_types.plain_description: A physician or other health care professional whose California license lets them do respirator medical evaluations and the medical exams some Cal/OSHA standards require. You choose the provider; TradeComply does not pick one.

when_required.situation: Before an employee is fit tested or first required to use a respirator, the employer must provide a medical evaluation, and must identify a physician or other licensed health care professional (PLHCP) to do it.

Employees required to use a respirator for silica 30 or more days a year must be offered medical surveillance at no cost, with every exam done by a PLHCP; the baseline exam is due within 30 days of assignment.
When the AQI for PM2.5 is over 500 (wildfire smoke), respirator use is required and respirators must be used under section 5144, which includes the medical evaluation.

extra_types.name: The operator of the high-voltage line (the utility that owns it)
extra_types.plain_description: The company that owns or operates the high-voltage line near your work, usually the electric utility. You notify it; only its own qualified electrical workers (or qualified persons using approved procedures) are exempt from the clearance rules.

when_required.situation: Before any work, materials or equipment come within the required clearance of an energized high-voltage line, the person responsible for the work must promptly notify the line's operator and complete the required safety measures first.

The clearance rules do not apply to qualified electrical workers authorized by the line's owner, or to qualified persons using approved equipment and procedures; everyone else must keep the clearances.

extra_types.verify_license_how: There is no license to look up: contact the company that owns or operates the line and keep a written record of the notice and the safety measures agreed.
bring_or_ask: Bring: the address, the equipment and its reach, the line voltage if known, and the dates.
Ask: Can the line be de-energized and grounded, or what other safety measures are required?
notes: No directory: the line operator is the company that owns or runs the line.

extra_types.name: Certified conveyance (elevator) mechanic and certified conveyance company
extra_types.plain_description: Elevator and other conveyance work is done by a Certified Competent Conveyance Mechanic (CCCM) employed by a Certified Qualified Conveyance Company (CQCC). Cal/OSHA's Elevator Unit certifies both.

when_required.situation: A conveyance mechanic must be certified (CCCM) and employed by a CQCC; a company that installs, alters, services or repairs conveyances must itself be certified (CQCC), which needs a current C-11 license.
when_required.legal_basis: Labor Code 7311.2, 7311.4 (as cited by DOSH); 8 CCR 344.30(h)

Ask: May we see your CQCC certificate and each mechanic's CCCM card?

extra_types.plain_description: A blaster holding a current California Blaster's License issued by Cal/OSHA. A licensed blaster must be physically on site to do or direct the blasting.

when_required.situation: No blasting may happen unless a blaster with a current, valid California Blaster's License from Cal/OSHA is physically on site to do or direct it; others may work under the licensed blaster's direct supervision.

extra_types.name: Air district-trained dust control person
extra_types.plain_description: Someone on your team (or hired by the owner) who has completed the air district's dust control class. In the South Coast district a large operation names a dust control supervisor; in the San Joaquin Valley a key person completes the District's Dust Control Training Class.

when_required.situation: A large operation in the South Coast district must identify a dust control supervisor, employed or hired by the owner or developer, who has completed the AQMD Fugitive Dust Control Class.

In the San Joaquin Valley, keep the approved Dust Control Plan on site, and at least one key person for the owner or operator, or whoever prepares the plan, must complete the District's Dust Control Training Class.

extra_types.name: Traffic control crew trained by an ATSSA-certified (or equivalent) supervisor
extra_types.plain_description: On a City of San Diego traffic control permit, every traffic control worker must be trained by a supervisor certified by the American Traffic Safety Services Association (ATSSA) or an equivalent.

when_required.situation: All traffic control workers under a City of San Diego traffic control permit must be trained by a supervisor certified by ATSSA (or equivalent), and the application must list every traffic control subcontractor with contact information.
when_required.legal_basis: City of San Diego Form DS-269 (June 2026), Requirements item 2

extra_types.verify_license_how: There is no state license to look up: ask the traffic control company for each worker's training record and the certifying supervisor's certification.
bring_or_ask: Bring: the traffic control plan and the permit application.
Ask: Who trained your crew, and what certification does that supervisor hold?
notes: ATSSA is a private association, not a government agency; TradeComply does not link to a training company.

handoffs.legal_basis_plain: Education Code 17280 and following (Field Act): not yet confirmed

handoffs.condition: Existing building: find out whether disturbed materials contain asbestos. Test: an item titled 'Asbestos survey of every material you will disturb'. The DOSH-certified consultant is required when the owner pays someone to survey or sample (B&P 7180.5); NESHAP's inspection duty covers a 'facility' (not homes of 4 or fewer units).
handoffs.test: any(i['title'].startswith('Asbestos survey of every material') for ph in result.phases for i in ph['items'])
handoffs.legal_basis: 40 CFR 61.145(a), 61.141 (inspection before demolition or renovation of a NESHAP facility); Labor Code 6501.9 (good-faith check before asbestos-related work; text read in the appendix of CSLB's 2022 Law Book on 2026-11-26); B&P 7180, 7180.5 DOSH certification (text read in the CSLB 2026 Law Book on 2026-11-26; the rulebook rules are still unchecked)

If the owner pays someone to survey or sample, that person must be certified by Cal/OSHA (DOSH) as an asbestos consultant.
handoffs.when_plain: Before the air district notice is due, or before work starts.
handoffs.legal_basis_plain: 40 CFR 61.145(a) and 61.141 (inspection before demolition or renovation of a building NESHAP covers); Labor Code 6501.9 (check for asbestos before the work; read in the appendix of CSLB's 2022 Law Book on 2026-11-26); B&P 7180, 7180.5 (DOSH certification; read in the CSLB 2026 Law Book on 2026-11-26, not yet confirmed in the rulebook)
